new_entities.name: Early egg introduction
new_entities.description: Introducing egg in infancy before or around 6 months of age for allergy prevention.

new_entities.name: Egg allergy prevention
new_entities.description: Lower risk of developing IgE-mediated egg allergy.

edges.effect_quant: A 2021 meta-analysis reported that introducing egg before 6 months reduced egg allergy risk versus later introduction (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.46-0.79), with an even stronger subgroup estimate in infants with allergic risk factors (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.40-0.75).
edges.population: infants, especially those with eczema or a family or personal predisposition to allergic disease
edges.mechanism: Early oral egg exposure may promote antigen-specific immune tolerance during a critical developmental window and reduce later allergic sensitization.
edges.summary: Early egg introduction is protective against later egg allergy overall, with the clearest benefit seen when introduced before 6 months in infants at elevated allergic risk.
edges.caveats: Form of egg, dose, and baseline eczema or sensitization status matter. Trials differ in whether they used heated, raw, or stepwise introduction strategies.

evidence.citation: Burgess JA et al 2019 Clin Exp Allergy
evidence.notes: Age at introduction to complementary solid food and food allergy and sensitization: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
